column1: # f70_map.tsv - the transliteration map D14's sweep is derived from.
# ONE authority (I2): f70_translit.py reads this file both to CONVERT and to
# VERIFY, so the sweep cannot drift from the map that documents it.
#   key          one or more codepoints, "U+XXXX" separated by spaces.  A
#                multi-codepoint key is matched FIRST (longest key wins), which
#                is how a damaged sequence is repaired as a unit instead of
#   replacement  literal ASCII.  <SP> = one space, <NONE> = delete.
#   note         why this replacement and not another.  A row without a note is
#                a guess, and a guess is not auditable.
# WHERE THE CHOICES COME FROM.  glibc's `iconv -t ASCII//TRANSLIT` is used as the
# baseline wherever it HAS an answer, so the row is grounded in a standard rather
# ">>" "|" "<=" "--" and "." , and plain "?" for the section sign, the degree
# sign and every Greek letter].  Two rows deviate from it DELIBERATELY, each with
# its argument in the note; every row it has no answer for is a choice, said out
# WHAT THIS MAP IS NOT APPLIED TO.  Inside a C-family STRING literal the sweep
# does not transliterate at all - it re-spells the same bytes as \xNN escapes, so
# the program's output does not move by one byte.  See f70_translit.py's header
# for that rule and its reason; the map governs comments and prose only.
# --- damaged sequences, repaired as a unit (these must match before singles) ---

column1: # --- symbols the standard has no answer for: choices, stated ---

column3: SECTION SIGN.  glibc gives "?".  "S11.169" stays readable as a section reference and costs one character; "sec." would cost four on 1134 occurrences

DEGREE SIGN.  glibc gives "?".  "deg" is what the unit is called; note that every degree sign that is PRINTED lives in a string literal and is escaped, not transliterated, so no on-screen angle changes

MIDDLE DOT.  glibc gives "." - DELIBERATE DEVIATION: every one of the 96 occurrences in the convert set is a multiplication or composition dot in a mathematical comment ("R'*(offset-free eye pos)", "Z(g1)*X(g2)*Z(g3)"), and "." would read as C++ member access at exactly those sites
superscript minus as the start of a negative exponent (the common pair is repaired whole above)
MODIFIER LETTER CAPITAL T: matrix transpose, written the way plain-text linear algebra writes it
COMBINING CIRCUMFLEX standing alone; the only real use, x-hat, is repaired whole above
BOX DRAWINGS LIGHT VERTICAL (glibc agrees); it appears only in PROSE DESCRIBING a drawn row, never in what is drawn
PROPORTIONAL TO: "~" is the plain-text idiom for proportionality, which is why "approximately" takes "~=" above
IDENTICAL TO: an identity, written as equality
LOGICAL AND, in a C++ comment about a boolean conjunction (OrbitModule.hpp:128)
SUPERSET OF, in "universe > milkyway > systems" (ssystem_factory.cpp:81) where it means containment
INTERSECTION, in "ray^sphere" (Camera.cpp:1120) - the plain-text operator for set intersection
square root, named rather than drawn
